analysis.title: Gridlock and diplomatic hopes lift US stocks (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: The S&P 500 closed 1.6% higher on Wednesday, reversing an initial negative futures reaction to Democrats taking control of both the House and the Senate. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.4%.
The 10-year US Treasury yield fell 8bps from its level before the election result. The DXY dollar index fell 0.5%.

Brent crude fell 8.2% overnight and stabilized around 95/bbl on hopes of US-Iran diplomacy. Qatar has stepped up mediation, but Iranian officials said a deal is possible only if the US accepts Iran's seven points.
Risk sentiment remains fragile in early Thursday trading. AI-heavy indices in South Korea and Taiwan were down 5.3% and 3.2%, and Nasdaq futures priced a 0.5% decline at the time of writing.

UBS says divided government makes abrupt changes to tax and spending policy harder to enact, since Trump retains the presidency and veto power. The S&P 500 gained an average of 15.5% in the six months after the previous 14 midterm elections since 1970, which UBS says is not a forecast.

Political risks remain: the next Congress must address government funding and the debt ceiling, which could raise bond market volatility. Trump retains broad executive authority over tariffs, foreign policy and regulation.

Democratic gains in key data center states such as Texas and Georgia could delay projects, raise costs or shift capacity location. On Wednesday large technology platforms rose while some data center construction names fell.

Investors are favoring financially strong platforms that fund investment from existing cash flow over businesses exposed to financing, construction, permitting or execution risk. UBS expects greater dispersion within technology.

Oil support: global inventories have fallen sharply, pledged strategic reserve releases are largely complete, and record freight costs, tight tanker capacity and recovering Chinese imports could keep prices elevated. Trump's comment that no military strike is imminent weighed on prices, but renewed military action remains a risk.
UBS recommends staying invested in diversified equities, preferring industrials, health care and financials, and regionally the Eurozone, emerging markets and Asia ex-Japan.

UBS recommends rebalancing concentrated technology exposure, favoring financially strong platforms and high-quality infrastructure providers, and keeping commodity exposure across energy, precious metals, industrial metals and agriculture as protection against geopolitical disruption.

The euro rose 0.4% against the dollar to around 1.12 and the dollar index slipped toward 101. Eurozone October headline inflation rose to 4.0% y/y from 3.8%, a three-year high. Core held at 2.5% and services rose to 3.3% from 3.2%. This reinforces expectations of an ECB hike in December.

UBS expects the dollar to stay under pressure and forecasts EURUSD at 1.16 by year-end. It notes crowded speculative dollar positioning could amplify a decline, and that congressional oversight of AI could weaken a capital flow tailwind for the dollar.

Per Bloomberg, Chinese AI and cloud developers ordered about 6 million NVIDIA RTX Pro 5500 chips, worth roughly USD 70bn. Buyers such as Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance reportedly expect only about 1% of orders over the next four months, with deliveries possibly reaching about 700,000 units by end-2027.

UBS forecasts aggregate AI capital spending of USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028, while noting investors are weighing overinvestment, financing and monetization risks more heavily.

trade_ideas.description: Reduce oversized single-stock technology positions into strength and diversify across the AI value chain, favoring financially strong platforms and high-quality infrastructure providers.
trade_ideas.rationale: Greater data center scrutiny and AI monetization questions could increase single-stock volatility.

trade_ideas.description: Hold broad commodity exposure across energy, precious metals, industrial metals and agriculture as protection against geopolitical disruption.
trade_ideas.rationale: Commodities can diversify portfolios when geopolitical disruption weighs on both stocks and bonds.

trade_ideas.description: Progressively reduce excess US dollar exposure, including shifting some dollar cash or fixed income into high-quality bonds in required currencies or selectively hedging currency exposure on US assets. UBS expects EURUSD at 1.16 by year-end.
trade_ideas.rationale: The dollar may stay under pressure after the election result, firmer Eurozone inflation and lower US yields.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy prices, European sovereign spreads and geopolitical developments could make the path volatile.

risk_factors: Breakdown in US-Iran negotiations or renewed attacks could push oil higher again.
Continued oil undersupply could deplete commercial stocks, with strategic reserve releases largely complete.
Government funding and debt ceiling negotiations could increase bond market volatility.
Democratic scrutiny of data center electricity use, water use and permitting could delay AI infrastructure projects.
Investor concerns about AI overinvestment, financing and monetization.
Executive authority over tariffs, foreign policy and regulation remains with Trump.
Crowded dollar positioning could amplify a dollar decline.
vol_and_positioning: Crowded speculative positioning in favor of the US dollar could amplify a dollar decline if UBS's expectations ease.
Nasdaq futures priced a 0.5% decline early Thursday after AI-heavy Korean and Taiwanese indices fell 5.3% and 3.2%.

UBS expects greater single-stock volatility from data center scrutiny and AI monetization questions, and potentially higher bond market volatility around government funding and debt ceiling negotiations.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: Qatar has stepped up mediation as Washington and Tehran appear to seek to resume talks, while Iran says a deal requires the US to accept its seven points.
Trump said no military strike is imminent, but renewed military action remains a risk, and it is unclear how long the US will support energy flows with military escorts.
US midterm elections: Democrats took both the House and the Senate, while Trump keeps the presidency and veto power.
US export restrictions limit China to less powerful AI chips such as the NVIDIA RTX Pro 5500.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong earnings, accelerating cloud revenue, expanding advance orders for compute capacity and large Chinese chip orders show AI demand remains robust, with UBS forecasting AI capex of USD 1.5tr by 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors are weighing overinvestment, financing and monetization risks, plus Democratic scrutiny of data centers, which favors cash-rich platforms and could raise single-stock volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Unspecified in the report, though UBS flags greater data center scrutiny and AI monetization questions as the factors that would raise single-stock volatility.

tension_points.bull_case: Qatar mediation and Trump's comment that no strike is imminent pushed Brent down 8.2% to around 95/bbl, with both sides having incentives to avoid a prolonged conflict.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran insists on its seven points, inventories have fallen sharply, strategic reserve releases are largely complete and freight costs are at records, so undersupply could support prices.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed attacks or a breakdown in negotiations could trigger another rise in oil prices.
